evidence_classes.DECODED DATA: ROM tables/records decoded by a parser
evidence_classes.BYTE-VERIFIED ASSEMBLY: routine bytes compared literally and disassembled by hand
evidence_classes.SOURCE-TRACED BEHAVIOR: behavior read from the disassembly, not executed
evidence_classes.CONTROLLED ROUTINE RESULT: original routine executed on a Z80 core with explicit RAM, swept over synthetic cameras
evidence_classes.EMULATED ORIGINAL FRAME: whole original game run in the approximate SMS harness

classes.A: WORLD-SPACE (canonical placement, terrain, level geometry, level limits)
classes.B: CAMERA-RELATIVE (a function of camera position or camera motion, not of the screen width)
classes.C: SCREEN-EDGE-RELATIVE (an offset from the left/right/centre of the original 256-px window)
classes.D: VIEWPORT/SPAWN-WINDOW-RELATIVE (create/sleep/delete bands around the camera window)
classes.G: PLAYER-RELATIVE WORLD DISTANCE (added by this audit: neither camera nor screen)

spawn_map.cell_index: col = (d + 128) >> 4, row = (dy + 128) >> 4; d + 128 must lie in 0..511 (8-bit after halving)

band_definition.0: d in [0,256): exactly the original 256-px window (rows: [0,256) too, taller than the 192-line screen)
band_definition.1: d in [-32,0) and [256,288): 32 px margin each side
band_definition.2: d in [-96,-32) and [288,352): 64 px outer ring
band_definition.3: d in [-128,-96) and [352,384), and anything outside [-128,384): deletion zone

level_limits.header_fields: act header +12 left, +14 top, +16 right, +18 bottom (words) -> $D280/$D27C/$D282/$D27E
level_limits.semantics: left is inclusive (camera >= left); right is EXCLUSIVE (camera < right, so the largest camera is right-1); right = world width - 256 in every THZ act (the 256 is the original window width encoded in data)

boss_tables.evidence: DECODED DATA (table bytes) + SOURCE-TRACED BEHAVIOR (use by the type $50 code); only zone 0 is exercised by a placed type
boss_tables.note: type $50 (THZ3 boss, zone 0) uses row 0: trigger |dx|<160,|dy|<256 from the PLAYER; pan target = boss anchor + (-256,-160), i.e. the boss anchor sits exactly on the original RIGHT edge (screen X 256) when the pan completes. Rows 1..6 are decoded but their users are other boss types whose code was not traced (UNRESOLVED).

unresolved: Whether the follow leads 104/136 were tuned to the 256-px width or are independent preferences; no ROM relation beyond the numbers.
Whether the player clamp literals 16 and 247 are intentionally mask(8)+extent(8) and 255-extent(8); the code uses literals, not extents.
Which boss types use pan-table rows 1..5 and trigger-table rows 1..5 (the table exists for zones 0..6; only zone 0 / type $50 is exercised).
Mechanics of the screen-relative sites in other zones' boss/object code (FUTURE_SITES); only instruction semantics are recorded.
Type $1C: writes absolute world X $C0..$DF / Y $20..$9F when screen X < $30; its coordinate frame and use are not traced.
Level-end camera relationship for zones 7/8 (special stages: right limits 7936/16128, bottom 16) not traced.
How the vertical constants (bottom limit = height - 240, bands 256 tall, pit death screen Y $D8) relate to 192/224/240-line modes.
Second camera-release step in the act-clear chain and what $0407 (freeze) does to follow after the results screen: the engine state is cleared by $4FCE.
Behaviour of $27 contact reach and POC-side widescreen choices are outside this audit.

lifetime_fixture.rule: cell = max(band(x-cam), band(y-camY)); cells 0/1 active; 2 asleep (bit 6 set); 3 or outside [-128,384) removed ($FE with placement token, $FF without) unless +$04 bit 1 keeps it asleep

placement_scan_fixture.rule: created iff occupancy byte is 0 and (cell == 2, or cell <= 1 while $D440 == 0 [initial fill]); record X/Y are stored world+256, so the test is (storedX-256-cam, storedY-256-camY); at most 11 slots; the scan runs once per 4 object updates

camera_follow_fixture.left_step_quirk: a step of exactly -8 is kept (A-B = $F8 passes the clamp), -9 and below become -7
camera_follow_fixture.rule: k = low byte of (playerX - $D284). k in [lead-8, lead+8] -> no scroll; k >= lead+8: +min(7, k-(lead+8)); k < lead-8: max(-7, k-(lead-8)) (exactly -8 allowed); the new target is $D174 + step

camera_pan_fixture.rule: each update: X += sign(targetX - camX), Y += sign(targetY - camY); moving right sets $D282 := targetX, moving left sets $D280 := targetX (not in zone index 6); pan mode ($D15F bit 0) persists after arrival and disables the follow routine

camera_limit_fixture.right_limit: EXCLUSIVE: camera < $D282, so the camera stops at $D282-1
camera_limit_fixture.overshoot_behaviour: a step that would cross the limit is dropped entirely (the camera does not slide to the limit)
camera_limit_fixture.consequence_for_sign_pan: pan target X = signX-$80 sets $D282 to the same value, hence the camera settles at signX-$81

player_edge_clamp_fixture.rule: e = low byte of (playerX - cam); e < $10 -> X = cam + $10; e >= $F8 -> X = cam + $F7; the snapped position is reduced by this update's X speed (8.8) and X speed is cleared; states >= $29 are not clamped by $4141. Player extents are NOT read.

state20_fixture.rule: d = (playerX - cameraX) as unsigned 16-bit: d > $F8 clears $D15E bit 7 and sets $D280 := camera (camera frozen); d > $120 (d >= $121 = 289 = RIGHT + 33) sets $D293 bit 5 (act index < 2) / bit 4; the 16-bit compare (unlike the clamp) allows d >= 256

child19_fixture.rule: created at X = cam + $104 (RIGHT + 4), Y = camY + $50; state 1 subtracts 8 per update until X <= cam + $85 (centre + 5); every term is relative to the camera at that update

player_distance_fixture.helper_rule: returns $FF iff |object - player| < BC (strict); independent of the camera for every camera swept
player_distance_fixture.type_28_rule: with +$04 bit 1 set: removed (type $FE) when |dx| >= $280 (640) or |dy| >= $2A0 (672) from the player

emulated_act_clear_camera.method: original ROM booted in tools/sms_frame_harness.py, camera/player placed at the stated start, RIGHT held until $D293 bit 4/5; frames counted from sign contact

emulated_bee_scroll.method: camera and player placed by the script every frame (camera scrolls right at a fixed rate, player at camera+104), THZ1 type $27 record (3504,224) in an otherwise untouched game

emulated_vdp.evidence: EMULATED ORIGINAL FRAME (VDP register state written by the original code)
emulated_vdp.note: R0 = $26 has bit 5 set. By SMS VDP documentation that masks screen column 0..7 with the backdrop colour, so the visible window is x = 8..255 of the 256-px scroll window. The mask is a hardware semantic of the register value, not measured on pixels here.
